text: You have a girlfriend and she posts revealing photos. How should you react? Hi, I've been watching your content for a while now, and I really respect the way you break down relationship situations in a balanced and honest way. I wanted to reach out because I'm dealing with something internally and I genuinely value your opinion. I've been with my girlfriend for about three months. Early in our relationship, she posted a few slightly revealing pictures, nothing extreme, just confident photos where she looks really good. I like how he calls them confident. At the time, I honestly wasn't bothered. I actually felt proud. I like that people could see how beautiful she is. I didn't feel disrespected. Well, in my opinion, it is fine for a man in a relationship to be bothered if his woman is revealing her body for other people to see. And I also think that it is normal in a relationship to have a healthy degree of possessiveness, both for men and for women. For me, it is actually a bit weird if people do not have that. But I've noticed something about myself that's starting to affect things. I have a bad habit of revisiting the past. I overthink things she's done before me, even though they have nothing to do with our relationship now. I also bring up mistakes she made earlier in our relationship, even after we talked about them, resolved them, and agreed to move forward. It is like I struggle to let things stay in the past. I keep reopening them in my mind and sometimes in conversations. Now I've even caught myself questioning those photos she posted, even though they didn't bother me at first. And I can tell if I genuinely have a boundary that I ignored in the beginning, or if I'm just creating insecurity because I tend to dwell on things. Again, I personally don't think it is an insecurity. If that bothers you, you need to talk about it. And if she keeps doing things that bother you afterwards, fine. It means you need another woman. Yes, there are plenty of women out there who would call you insecure, possessive, and so on for this kind of stuff. But there are also plenty of women who would be fine with this boundary. You just need to find what works for you. So you could be enjoying your relationship instead of worrying about it. Now about the past. Plenty of guys are bothered by the girl's past. You do not give details here, so it is hard for me to give my opinion. At the end of the day, the decision goes like this. You can't let it go. You break up and move on. Or if it's nothing serious really and her current actions show you she's a good girlfriend, then you keep going with the relationship. So I really want your opinion. What do you think about partners posting slightly revealing photos while in a relationship? Is that something I should naturally feel bothered by? Or is this more about my insecurity and overthinking? I already answered this. I think it is completely normal for a man in a relationship to be bothered by it. I don't want to control her or project my internal struggles onto her. At the same time, I don't want to suppress something if it is a valid boundary. I'm trying to figure out the difference between having standards and just being insecure. Well, this is an interesting topic. To understand it, you need experience and common sense. I try to convey my vision of those things through my channel. If you want a shortcut, just listen to yourself. If your gut feeling tells you something is wrong, it is normally correct. So if the revealing photos bother you, you talk to your girlfriend about it and her actions will be your answer. I care about her and I don't want to sabotage something good because I can't seem to let go of the past. I genuinely want to grow and become more secure, not keep reopening wounds that should already be healed. I'd really appreciate your perspective on both the revealing photos topic and why someone might struggle to move on from past mistakes in a relationship. Thank you for your content. It helped me reflect on myself a lot. Again, you don't exactly specify what past mistakes were. Generally, what you do is you learn from mistakes in your past, in your previous relationships, and you try not to do them in your future relationships. I gave my other comments along the way. I hope it was helpful. Hope it was informative. Thanks a lot. My name is Ilyas Abdullin and bye.
